If you visited the Zoo... Log In Forgot Account? Mesker Park Zoo & Botanic Garden's Post Mesker Park Zoo & Botanic Garden 2d · Meet the newest addition to our François langur monkey troop, Fern. Fern was born early last week to first-time mom Ta-Shi. If you visited the Zoo around that time, you may have noticed that the Discovery Center was temporarily closed. This was due to our animal care team needing to intervene to help Ta-Shi get comfortable in her new role as a mom, in hopes of saving Fern’s life. When staff arrived, Ta-Shi was not providing all the care needed for her newborn. Our team immediately stepped in to provide supplemental care. At the same time, we consulted with the François langur Species Survival Plan to learn how other AZA-accredited zoos have successfully handled similar situations to give Fern and Ta-Shi the best chance of bonding successfully. Hand rearing of this species is an absolute last resort, and our goal was for Fern to be reared by her mother with the help of the other langur females in the troop. Our animal care team worked around the clock, including staying overnight at the Zoo to provide supplemental feedings. Fern and Ta-Shi were moved to a smaller, quiet space equipped with a camera so they could be observed 24/7, all in hopes that Ta-Shi would bond with Fern and begin nursing. After a long 48 hours, Ta-Shi began carrying and holding Fern for longer periods of time and nursing her consistently. Following continued successful observations of nursing and maternal care, Fern and Ta-Shi were slowly reintroduced to the rest of the troop. Today, the entire troop is back together, and baby Fern is doing great! When visiting our new resident, please be sure to keep your volume low so as not to disrupt this exciting addition to the Mesker Park Zoo... (truncated)
